scope: Same complete 81-path review scope, all 112 obligations and ten shared scopes.

semantic_notes: QuickSort value and accumulator base/step/permutation interfaces retain arbitrary Boolean comparators and arbitrary payloads. The accumulator suffix is carried unchanged through the right recursion; key wrappers require only decidable LT for construction.

Top-down sortFloorBy explicitly takes and drops floor(length/2), returns short lists unchanged, and preserves permutation, length and membership without order laws. Sortedness requires only a key preorder and the stated input-local compatibility of both comparator branches.

The key-specific top-down correctness result uses a linear preorder; stability and StableSort separately add key equality. Equality to sortOn uses a linear order and key equality, not an unstated payload equality or an inference that sortedness alone implies stability.

Appendix C composition, Bool/Prop truth, list comprehension order/repetition, set image/comprehension/union/intersection, strict subset, products and bounded quantifier elaborations agree with their stated correspondence roles. The identical elaborated bounded-quantifier sides are intentional notation correspondence.

All six interval membership equivalences require only a preorder and preserve endpoint directions; the concrete upper-interval example distinguishes Iic from Ici. Int floor division equals ordinary Int division for nonnegative divisor, with explicit negative-divisor5/(-2)=-3 versus -2 and divisor-zero value0; typed arithmetic distinguishes Nat division from Real division.
Floor/ceiling of -3/2 are respectively -2/-1. Multiset support inclusion explicitly fails to imply multiplicity order; list/multiset repeated sums/products differ from Finset folds as intended.

The closed finite interval fold includes both endpoints. finiteIndexProduct requires only CommMonoid and uses the finite index set convention: finite sets use toFinset, infinite index sets return1 even for functions with finite exceptional support. Its sum counterpart returns0 on the infinite-index example. This is the recorded source convention, not a claim about infinite analytic products or sums.
Empty index type is supported without Inhabited. Ordered list fold concatenation needs only Monoid/AddMonoid, preserving noncommutative order rather than introducing commutativity.
Insertion examples retain empty cost1, arbitrary singleton cost3, sorted-with-duplicates cost7, descending-three worst10 and the global lower/triangular/quadratic bounds.

Concrete insertion results distinguish immediate tied-head cost1, full traversal cost4 and early tied-head exit despite an unsorted tail. The keyed record StableSort contract remains generic over arbitrary payload types.
